q: Bugey's Cerdon cru makes essentially one wine. Which is it?
opts: A sweet pink sparkler from Gamay and Poulsard, méthode ancestrale
A dry white sparkler from Jacquère and Altesse, traditional method
A dry rosé sparkler from Mondeuse and Gamay, traditional method
A sweet white sparkler from Altesse and Molette, méthode ancestrale
exp: Bugey, between Savoie and the Jura, became an AOC in 2009, and Cerdon is its calling card: a single fermentation stopped by chilling and filtration with sugar still unfermented, bottled at roughly 8% alcohol and 40-plus g/L of residual sugar. Gamay leads with Poulsard alongside — the Jura's grape appearing on the Savoyard side of the line. The traditional-method distractors are the trap: any second fermentation would take it dry and lose the point.

q: Nada's 'miyamizu' water makes what style, versus Fushimi's soft water?
accept: hard water robust dry vs soft gentle
ans: Nada (Kobe): mineral-hard water, robust dry sake; Fushimi (Kyoto): soft water, gentler style

q: What two legal conditions define a French Vin Doux Naturel?
accept: 252 g/l minimum must and mutage with 96 percent grape spirit
fortified with neutral grape spirit at five to ten percent of volume
minimum 252 grams of natural sugar then mutage
mutage with 96% spirit at 5 to 10 percent
ans: The must must reach at least 252 g/L of natural sugar, and fermentation is arrested by mutage — the addition of neutral grape spirit of at least 96% abv, at between 5 and 10 per cent of the volume
exp: The name is a trap: nothing about a vin doux naturel is unfortified. What is 'natural' is the sugar, which must all come from the grape — no chaptalisation, no sweetening — hence the high minimum must weight. The 5–10% spirit band separates VDN from Port, which takes a larger addition of lower-strength spirit. The family covers Banyuls, Maury, Rivesaltes, Rasteau and the Muscats of Beaumes-de-Venise, Rivesaltes, Frontignan and Saint-Jean-de-Minervois.

q: Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise is a vin doux naturel. Describe how it is made and the sweetness the law demands.
accept: mutage with neutral grape spirit stops the fermentation leaving 110 grams of sugar
fortified mid-ferment so a minimum 110 g/l residual sugar remains at about 15 percent
muscat blanc a petits grains fortified with grape spirit vin doux naturel style
arrested fermentation by adding spirit minimum 110 grams per litre residual sugar
ans: Fermentation is arrested by mutage — neutral grape spirit at around 96% is added to kill the yeast — leaving a minimum 110 grams per litre of residual sugar at roughly 15% alcohol, made from Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains and its coloured mutations
exp: 'Naturel' refers to the sugar being the grape's own rather than added, not to the spirit — the mutage is exactly what makes it a VDN rather than a late-harvest wine. The same mechanism runs Rasteau and Banyuls; what differs is the timing of the addition and whether the skins are still in the vat when it happens.
